note: Source-of-truth for the scheduled 'After the Close' blog drip. Each post is published from _scheduled/atc/<slug>.html into blog/<slug>.html on its date by _scripts/publish_scheduled.py (run daily by .github/workflows/scheduled-publish.yml). Edit a post's source here before its date and the change is picked up automatically. Posts are ordered by date.

posts.title: Who Owns the So-What After the Books Close?
posts.card_desc: Your software can close the books in a day. It still can't tell you what the numbers mean or what to do Monday morning. Here's who owns the so-what.
posts.llms_desc: After your books close, who owns the so-what? Why automation produces output but judgment — naming the one number that matters and the next move — is still human work. Opener of the After the Close series.

posts.title: Your Real Bottleneck Is Hours, Not Tools
posts.card_desc: The best operators already have the tools and the data. Their scarce resource is hours and judgment. Why a finance partner, not more software, is the fix.
posts.llms_desc: The strongest operators already have tools and data; their bottleneck is hours and judgment load. Why the fix is a finance partner, not more software.

posts.title: Does Your Finance Partner Know Where You're Going?
posts.card_desc: Most finance work stops at the company and never reaches the founder. Why finance tied to your long-term security is the half that actually matters.
posts.llms_desc: Finance that stops at the company misses the founder. Tying growth to the owner's long-term security, distributions, and timeline — the half of finance most partners skip.

posts.title: Why Growth Is What Breaks Your Cash
posts.card_desc: Fast growth widens the gap between cash out and cash in. Why your cash conversion cycle, not revenue, decides whether you survive your own growth.
posts.llms_desc: Why fast growth breaks cash: the cash conversion cycle, working capital, and the float gap that revenue growth widens. The metric that decides whether you survive scaling.

posts.title: Your Blended ROAS Is Hiding Your Best Channel
posts.card_desc: A blended ROAS average looks healthy while it protects your worst channel and starves your best. How to break it apart by channel and payback window.
posts.llms_desc: Blended ROAS hides your best channel and protects your worst. Breaking marketing performance apart by channel and payback window to fund what actually pays back.

posts.title: The Custom AI Build the Platform Makes Free
posts.card_desc: The custom AI you build today the platform may hand you free six months later. The finance question to ask before you spend on a bespoke build.
posts.llms_desc: The custom AI build the platform makes free six months later — the finance framing for build-vs-wait decisions on bespoke AI systems.

posts.title: Lead With Your Scar, Not Your Resume
posts.card_desc: Founders trust shared scars, not credentials. Why a five-year inventory mistake earns more trust than any track record, and what that means for finance.
posts.llms_desc: Founders trust scars over resumes. Why leading with a hard, specific failure builds more trust than credentials — and what that means for how finance shows up. Close of the After the Close series.
